chronology.event: Joins the Canadian Department of Transport
Establishes Canada's far north ionospheric monitoring system
At the NARBA conference learns from Dr Robert Sarbacher of the US classification of the saucer question and of Vannevar Bush's role
Writes the 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications, Department of Transport; classified Top Secret
Project Magnet report concludes the vehicles are 'probably extra-terrestrial' and recommends acquisition of the technology
Establishes the Shirley's Bay observatory outside Ottawa
Department of Transport terminates Project Magnet funding; Smith continues privately
The 1950 memorandum downgraded from Top Secret to Confidential

After his return to Canada, Smith wrote a memo dated November 21, 1950 which became classified Top Secret until being downgraded to Confidential in 1969.'

This was called Project Magnet ... Unable to convince his colleagues of the merits of his research, Smith had to continue his work privately after the Department of Transport terminated Project Magnet in 1954.'

label: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith
narrative: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith (1910 - 27 December 1962) is the earliest named government official anywhere on record to have been told, and to have written down, that the American flying saucer question was classified above the hydrogen bomb and was being run by Vannevar Bush. Smith joined the Canadian Department of Transport in 1939, built Canada's far north ionospheric monitoring system in 1947, and was Canada's chief delegate to the North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement conferences of 1949 and 1950; by 1952 he was Senior Radio Engineer of the DOT's Broadcast and Measurements section, and in 1957 became Superintendent of Radio Regulations Engineering. At the 1950 NARBA conference in Washington he made enquiries of the American scientist Dr Robert Sarbacher and came away with four assertions which he set down in a memorandum, 'Geo-Magnetics', addressed to the Controller of Telecommunications and dated 21 November 1950: that the matter was the most highly classified subject in the United States government, rating higher even than the H-bomb; that flying saucers exist; that their modus operandi was unknown but that a concentrated effort was being made by a small group headed by Doctor Vannevar Bush; and that the entire matter was considered by US authorities to be of tremendous significance. That memorandum was classified Top Secret and was not downgraded to Confidential until 1969. Library and Archives Canada quotes the same memorandum in its own online exhibition: 'the existence of a different technology is borne out by the investigations which are being carried on at the present time in relation to flying saucers ... I feel that the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence.' The memorandum was the successful request that produced Project Magnet.

timeline.label: Smith writes the 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum
timeline.text: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith, Senior Radio Engineer of the Canadian Department of Transport, writes a Top Secret memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications recording what he had been told in Washington: that the flying saucer question was the most highly classified subject in the United States government, rating higher than the H-bomb, and was being worked by a small group headed by Vannevar Bush. Library and Archives Canada quotes the same memorandum's operative line: 'the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence'.

unverified: The four-point passage of the 21 November 1950 memorandum ('rating higher even than the H-bomb'; 'Flying saucers exist'; 'a small group headed by Doctor Vannevar Bush'; 'of tremendous significance') is universally reproduced in the literature but the exact Library and Archives Canada file citation for the memorandum itself was not confirmed in this pass. Researchers commonly cite Department of Transport records in RG 97; LAC's own exhibition cites Project Magnet material at RG 24, acc. 83-84/167, box 7523, file DRBS 3800-10-1, pt.1, which is the Defence Research Board file. The DOT file reference must be confirmed at LAC before the four-point quotation is used as tier 1.
Whether Robert Sarbacher's account to Smith was ever corroborated by Sarbacher in writing was not established in this pass.
